c1-05-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Say It With a Smile
c1-05-01.scenario: At a meeting, a colleague says the new report is perfect, although everyone knows it has mistakes.
c1-05-01.prompt: Answer with irony, as if you agreed.
cues: Hint that nobody has read it
c1-05-01.target: A jelentés, ugyebár, mindenben rendben van. Elvégre senki sem olvasta el.
c1-05-01.english: The report is fine in every way, mind you. After all, nobody has read it.
c1-05-01.canDo: I can make a remark ironic with *elvégre* and *netalán*.

c1-05-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Not Exactly a Success
c1-05-02.scenario: A colleague shows you a plan that went wrong and asks for your opinion.
c1-05-02.prompt: Say politely but clearly that the plan was not a success.
cues: Soften the start with 'to put it mildly'
Say that it was not a good plan
c1-05-02.target: A terv, enyhén szólva, nem volt a legjobb.
c1-05-02.english: The plan, to put it mildly, was not the best.
c1-05-02.canDo: I can soften a criticism with *enyhén szólva* and litotes (*nem éppen a legjobb*).

c1-05-03.title: Communicative Challenge: With All Due Respect
c1-05-03.scenario: At a meeting, the speaker says his plan is perfect. You see that the numbers are wrong.
c1-05-03.prompt: Start politely, then say what is wrong.
cues: Say that the numbers are not right
c1-05-03.target: Minden tiszteletem mellett bátorkodom megjegyezni, hogy a számok nem jók.
c1-05-03.english: With all due respect, I venture to remark that the numbers are not right.
c1-05-03.canDo: I can open a sharp objection with *minden tiszteletem mellett* or *bátorkodom megjegyezni*.

c1-05-04.title: Communicative Challenge: In Plain Words
c1-05-04.scenario: An office announces a 'temporary reorganisation'. You and a colleague know that the project is dead, and the colleague asks what the phrase means.
c1-05-04.prompt: Say in plain words what the office phrase means.
cues: Say that the money has run out
c1-05-04.english: In plain words: the money has run out.
c1-05-04.canDo: I can unmask an official euphemism in plain words with *magyarán szólva*.

c1-05-05.title: Communicative Challenge: What Does the Text Say?
c1-05-05.scenario: You have read a short text about István Örkény. A friend asks what it says about the grotesque.
c1-05-05.prompt: Tell your friend what the text says about laughter.
cues: Say what the grotesque helps with
c1-05-05.target: A szöveg szerint a groteszk segít túlélni, mert a nevetés megvéd a félelemtől.
c1-05-05.english: According to the text, the grotesque helps people survive, because laughter protects against fear.
c1-05-05.canDo: I can say what the text about Örkény says about the grotesque and the *Egyperces novellák*.

c1-05-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Irony, Then Respect
c1-05-consolidation.scenario: After a meeting, you tell a colleague about the boss's report, first ironically, then politely.
c1-05-consolidation.prompt: Be ironic about the report, then disagree politely.
cues: Mock the report with an irony particle
c1-05-consolidation.target: A jelentés, ugyebár, mindenben rendben van. Minden tiszteletem mellett bátorkodom megjegyezni, hogy nincs.
c1-05-consolidation.english: The report is fine in every way, mind you. With all due respect, I venture to remark that it is not.
c1-05-consolidation.canDo: I can make a remark ironic with *ugyebár*, *elvégre* or *netalán*.
